opening.text: Imagine a hiker with a map in the backpack who never opens it. The map is right there. But it helps no one if it stays closed.
The scriptures are a map for life. Today I want to talk about opening it.

mainMessage.text: The scriptures are God’s words to us. They point to Jesus Christ, they teach us what to do, and they help us feel the Spirit. They work best when we study them every day, ask questions, and apply what we learn.

blocks.text: A map that points to Christ.
The Savior said the scriptures testify of Him. Nephi said the words of Christ will tell us what to do.

Angels speak by the power of the Holy Ghost; wherefore, they speak the words of Christ. Wherefore, I said unto you, feast upon the words of Christ; for behold, the words of Christ will tell you all things what ye should do.
Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Blessing of Scripture” from the April 2010 general conference.
The central purpose of all scripture is to fill our souls with faith in God the Father and in His Son, Jesus Christ.
Every page leads back to Him.
A light for the mind.
Paul told Timothy that the scriptures make us wise and ready for good works. He told the Romans that they give us hope.

And that from a child thou hast known the holy scriptures, which are able to make thee wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus. All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: That the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works.
For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.
Elder Richard G. Scott of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Power of Scripture” from the October 2011 general conference.
Scriptures are like packets of light that illuminate our minds and give place to guidance and inspiration from on high.
Light helps us see the next step.
A little each day.
The people of Berea searched the scriptures daily. Joshua was told to keep the book on his lips and to think on it day and night.
These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.

This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.
President Ezra Taft Benson said this in his talk “The Power of the Word” from the April 1986 general conference.

One of the most important things you can do . . . is to immerse yourselves in the scriptures. Search them diligently. Feast upon the words of Christ. Learn the doctrine. Master the principles that are found therein.
Small steps still cover many miles.
Read with the Spirit.
On the road to Emmaus, two disciples felt their hearts burn as Jesus Christ opened the scriptures to them. The Lord tells us to seek first to obtain His word.
And they said one to another, Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the scriptures?

Seek not to declare my word, but first seek to obtain my word, and then shall your tongue be loosed; then, if you desire, you shall have my Spirit and my word, yea, the power of God unto the convincing of men.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Blessing of Scripture” from the April 2010 general conference.
Faith comes by the witness of the Holy Spirit to our souls, Spirit to spirit, as we hear or read the word of God.
The Spirit turns words into understanding.
Make it personal.
Nephi compared the scriptures to his own family so they would help them. James told us to do what the word says, not only hear it.

And I did read many things unto them which were written in the books of Moses; but that I might more fully persuade them to believe in the Lord their Redeemer I did read unto them that which was written by the prophet Isaiah; for I did liken all scriptures unto us, that it might be for our profit and learning.
But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.
President Ezra Taft Benson said this in his talk “The Book of Mormon—Keystone of Our Religion” from the October 1986 general conference.

If they saw our day, and chose those things which would be of greatest worth to us, is not that how we should study the Book of Mormon? We should constantly ask ourselves, ‘Why did the Lord inspire Mormon (or Moroni or Alma) to include that in his record? What lesson can I learn from that to help me live in this day and age?’
Ask what it means for you.
Effort brings power.
The sons of Mosiah searched the scriptures diligently, and they grew strong in the truth. Helaman taught that the word of God can guide us safely through the traps of the devil.

Now these sons of Mosiah were with Alma at the time the angel first appeared unto him; therefore Alma did rejoice exceedingly to see his brethren; and what added more to his joy, they were still his brethren in the Lord; yea, and they had waxed strong in the knowledge of the truth; for they were men of a sound understanding and they had searched the scriptures diligently, that they might know the word of God.

Yea, we see that whosoever will may lay hold upon the word of God, which is quick and powerful, which shall divide asunder all the cunning and the snares and the wiles of the devil, and lead the man of Christ in a strait and narrow course across that everlasting gulf of misery which is prepared to engulf the wicked— And land their souls, yea, their immortal souls, at the right hand of God in the kingdom of heaven, to sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and with Jacob, and with all our holy fathers, to go no more out.
Elder David A. Bednar of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Watching with All Perseverance” from the April 2010 general conference.

Spiritual understanding . . . simply cannot be given to \[us\]. The tuition of diligence and of learning by study and also by faith must be paid to obtain and personally ‘own’ such knowledge. Only in this way can what is known in the mind also be felt in the heart.
The map only works when we use it.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time a scripture helped them. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Understandest thou what thou readest?

blocks.text: A man from Ethiopia was riding in his chariot, reading the prophet Isaiah. Philip came alongside.

And Philip ran thither to him, and heard him read the prophet Esaias, and said, Understandest thou what thou readest? And he said, How can I, except some man should guide me? And he desired Philip that he would come up and sit with him.
The man was reading, but he did not yet understand. He was glad to be helped. We all need help at times. We can pray, ask a teacher, or use study helps. Asking is part of learning.

application.text: First, choose a time each day to read the scriptures, even if it is only five minutes. Second, mark one verse that stands out to you. Third, write down what it means for your life.

story.title: Of great worth unto us

blocks.text: Nephi and his brothers brought the brass plates out of Jerusalem at great cost. Then they read them.

And we had obtained the records which the Lord had commanded us, and searched them and found that they were desirable; yea, even of great worth unto us, insomuch that we could preserve the commandments of the Lord unto our children.
They treated the scriptures like treasure. They carried them through the wilderness and taught from them. Our own copy deserves the same care.

story.title: Every word of God

blocks.text: After a long fast, Jesus Christ was tempted to turn stones into bread. He answered with scripture.
But he answered and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.
He did not argue. He quoted the words of God. The scriptures gave Him strength when He was hungry and tired. They can do the same for us.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time reading together brought understanding. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: They gave the sense

blocks.text: After the people returned to Jerusalem, Ezra and the Levites read the law of God to them.
So they read in the book in the law of God distinctly, and gave the sense, and caused them to understand the reading.
They read clearly, and then they explained it. The people understood, and they rejoiced. Reading together, and talking about what we read, can bring that same light into a home.

application.text: First, read a few verses aloud with your family or a friend. Second, pause and ask what one verse means. Third, thank God for the light.

A well is not for one drink a month. The Bereans searched the scriptures daily. Joshua was told to think on the book day and night.
These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.

This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.
President Ezra Taft Benson said this in his talk “The Power of the Word” from the April 1986 general conference.

One of the most important things you can do . . . is to immerse yourselves in the scriptures. Search them diligently. Feast upon the words of Christ. Learn the doctrine. Master the principles that are found therein.
A little water each day keeps us from thirst.
The Spirit lowers the bucket.
We cannot reach the deepest water alone. The two disciples on the road felt their hearts burn as Jesus opened the scriptures. The Lord says to seek first to obtain His word.
And they said one to another, Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the scriptures?

Seek not to declare my word, but first seek to obtain my word, and then shall your tongue be loosed; then, if you desire, you shall have my Spirit and my word, yea, the power of God unto the convincing of men.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Blessing of Scripture” from the April 2010 general conference.
Faith comes by the witness of the Holy Spirit to our souls, Spirit to spirit, as we hear or read the word of God.
The Spirit brings the water up.
Drink it in.
Water helps only when we drink it. Nephi applied the scriptures to his own family. James told us to do what the word says.

And I did read many things unto them which were written in the books of Moses; but that I might more fully persuade them to believe in the Lord their Redeemer I did read unto them that which was written by the prophet Isaiah; for I did liken all scriptures unto us, that it might be for our profit and learning.
But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.
President Ezra Taft Benson said this in his talk “The Book of Mormon—Keystone of Our Religion” from the October 1986 general conference.

If they saw our day, and chose those things which would be of greatest worth to us, is not that how we should study the Book of Mormon? We should constantly ask ourselves, ‘Why did the Lord inspire Mormon (or Moroni or Alma) to include that in his record? What lesson can I learn from that to help me live in this day and age?’
What we drink becomes part of us.
A deeper well each year.
The more we draw, the more we find. The sons of Mosiah studied diligently and grew strong. Helaman said the word of God can lead us safely past the traps of the adversary.

Now these sons of Mosiah were with Alma at the time the angel first appeared unto him; therefore Alma did rejoice exceedingly to see his brethren; and what added more to his joy, they were still his brethren in the Lord; yea, and they had waxed strong in the knowledge of the truth; for they were men of a sound understanding and they had searched the scriptures diligently, that they might know the word of God.

Yea, we see that whosoever will may lay hold upon the word of God, which is quick and powerful, which shall divide asunder all the cunning and the snares and the wiles of the devil, and lead the man of Christ in a strait and narrow course across that everlasting gulf of misery which is prepared to engulf the wicked— And land their souls, yea, their immortal souls, at the right hand of God in the kingdom of heaven, to sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and with Jacob, and with all our holy fathers, to go no more out.
Elder David A. Bednar of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Watching with All Perseverance” from the April 2010 general conference.

Spiritual understanding . . . simply cannot be given to \[us\]. The tuition of diligence and of learning by study and also by faith must be paid to obtain and personally ‘own’ such knowledge. Only in this way can what is known in the mind also be felt in the heart.
The effort is worth it.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time one verse spoke to them with power. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Never did any passage of scripture come with more power

blocks.text: Joseph Smith was a young man with a big question. He read a verse in the book of James.

Never did any passage of scripture come with more power to the heart of man than this did at this time to mine. It seemed to enter with great force into every feeling of my heart. I reflected on it again and again, knowing that if any person needed wisdom from God, I did; for how to act I did not know, and unless I could get more wisdom than I then had, I would never know; for the teachers of religion of the different sects understood the same passages of scripture so differently as to destroy all confidence in settling the question by an appeal to the Bible.
One verse, read with a sincere heart, spoke to him. He thought about it again and again. Then he acted on it. That is how the water reaches us.

application.text: First, read again the verse that spoke to you most this month. Second, write down one question and look for an answer in the scriptures. Third, act on one thing you learn.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that the scriptures are a well that never runs dry. I know the water comes from Jesus Christ. I know that the Spirit helps us drink. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.
